Name: Anthony Nunez
Report: Nunez is a converted infielder who raced to the big leagues in just a couple of pro seaons as a picher. He has rare repertoire depth for a reliever and might eventually parlay that into a starting role.

Name: Kevin Alcántara
Report: Long, lanky, and loaded with tools and projection, Alcántara is a loose, 6-foot-6 outfielder with massive potential but also plenty of hit tool risk.

Name: Seth Johnson
Report: Johnson's plus stuff always impressed more than the results during his tenure at Campbell, but the Rays might be the perfect team to help him weaponize it.

Name: Jairo Iriarte
Report: Iriarte has plus stuff and the athleticism and fluidity to improve his control with time.

Name: Owen Caissie
Report: Elite power makes Caissie's K-prone skill set viable in an outfield corner.

Name: Kyle Hurt
Report: Hurt's changeup and ability to land his breaking ball for strikes gives him a shot to start despite his bulk and mechanical violence.

Name: Zac Veen
Report: Veen's lefty swing is still vulnerable to inner-half velocity, and he remains in a liminal prospect space more than he is a slam dunk big league star.

Name: Shane Drohan
Report: Drohan made changes to his repertoire and uage in 2025 (new cutter, slower slider, threw more breakers than changeups) and cut his walk rate significantly compared to '23-'24. He looks like a good swingman now.

Name: Cristian Mena
Report: Mena is an athletic starter with good secondary stuff and precocious command.

Name: Jeferson Quero
Report: Quero has plus bat speed and arm strength, but a volatile approach.

Name: Winston Santos
Report: Santos is an athletic, strike-throwing starter with a mid-90s fastball, but pedestrian secondary stuff.

Name: Angel Genao
Report: Genao is a well-rounded shortstop who is still growing into meaningful power.

Name: Moisés Ballesteros
Report: Ballesteros can really hit. Defensively, well, he can really hit.

Name: Samuel Basallo
Report: Basallo has a plus throwing arm and top of the scale power that he's gotten to consistently in the minors, but his plate approach and ball blocking still need work.

Name: Yilber Díaz
Report: A supreme little athlete, Diaz has three plus pitches and demonstrated in 2024 that he could sustain upper-90s velocity across more than 100 innings. He should polish his command enough to be a mid-rotation starter at peak, and if he can't, he'll still be a really nasty late-inning reliever.

Name: Carter Jensen
Report: Jensen is a power-hitting lefty catcher who squares up the ball as reliably as any prospect in the game. He projects to grow into an average defender and is big-league ready.

Name: River Ryan
Report: Ryan looked like an impact starter before injuries ended his 2024 and wiped out his 2025.

Name: Joe Mack
Report: Mack is a power-hitting lefty catcher with a plus-plus arm. A long swing and corresponding hit risk likely pushes him to the back of the batting order.

Name: James Triantos
Report: Triantos raked in high school then allayed any concerns that he lacked pro physicality by continuing to do so upon his entry into affiliated ball.

Name: Chayce McDermott
Report: McDermott has struggled with walks, but he'll show you four plus pitches and his athleticism indicates the command might arrive late.

Name: Bubba Chandler
Report: Chandler's command and slider consistency are pretty raw, but his athleticism and background (former multi-sport & two-way player) allow for projection in these areas. He has prototypical size and arm strength, and his changeup has improved a ton as a pro. He's a potential front end arm.

Name: Tanner McDougal
Report: McDougal is a big-bodied right-hander with plus velocity and two bat-missing breaking balls. His lack of changeup feel and delivery effort pose substantial relief risk.

Name: Edwin Arroyo
Report: Still on the 2B/SS line, the lift in Arroyo's swing helps him get to impact power for a middle infielder.

Name: Harry Ford
Report: Ford is a laser-armed catcher who, brick-by-brick, has become a major league-quality receiver. Selectivity at the dish helps him do enough to be a primary catcher.

Name: McCade Brown
Report: Brown changed his delivery in 2025 (his placement on the rubber, his stride direction) and broke out. He's a fastball-heavy no. 4/5 starter with more ceiling than that if he can develop a changeup later than most. His injury history has cost him reps, so maybe the cambio will improve as he gains experience.

Name: Carson Williams
Report: Williams has plus power and a potential 70-grade glove at short, but there's enough swing-and-miss that there's more bust potential than his FV grade would normally suggest.

Name: Andrew Painter
Report: Painter struggled to locate his secondary stuff for chase in 2025. He had a good season for a player his age at Triple-A, but didn't dominate and kick down the door to the bigs as hoped. Can he bounce back in 2026, or is he going to be just okay?

Name: Chase Petty
Report: Petty is a phenomenal athlete who altered his approach to pitching in 2024.

Name: Didier Fuentes
Report: Fuentes has been promoted quickly, and perhaps wasn't ready for his big league debut. A good fastball, well-rounded mix, and projectable command give him mid-rotation upside.

Name: Jimmy Crooks
Report: Crooks is a polished defensive catcher with a below-average bat, but he offers the brute strength to produce double-digit home run seasons.

Name: Logan Henderson
Report: Henderson is a ready-made no. 4 starter with a modern pitcher's arsenal, headlined by a carrying fastball.

Name: Sal Stewart
Report: Other than pulling fastballs, Stewart does everything well at the plate, which should allow him to be a regular at first base, his likely defensive home.

Name: Alex Freeland
Report: After strikeouts plagued the early portion of his pro career, Freeland had a breakout 2024 and now looks like a soon-to-be everyday shortstop.

Name: Dylan Beavers
Report: Beavers is a corner outfielder with power and a good approach. Long levers and a tendency to work deep counts may limit his ability to hit for average.

Name: JR Ritchie
Report: The arm strength scouts have been projecting Ritchie to develop arrived last year. He's a near-ready no. 3/4 starter.

Name: Elmer Rodríguez
Report: Rodríguez projects as a mid-rotation starter, largely on his ability to generate groundballs with his sinker.

Name: Robby Snelling
Report: Snelling went to a third party facility and changed his delivery, then had a proper breakout in 2025. He's now on track to be in Miami's rotation during the next year or so.

Name: Parker Messick
Report: Messick has profiled as a low-variance no. 4 lefty starter with a plus changeup for a while now, and he looked the part during his seven-start debut in 2025.

Name: Noah Schultz
Report: Schultz was troubled by patellar tendinitis in 2025 and has a checkered health history, but he has largely thrown strikes and touts a plus slider from a freaky XL left-handed frame.

Name: Chase DeLauter
Report: A litany of injuries have made it tough for DeLauter to stay on the field. When he's healthy, he looks like a heart-of-the-order bat capable of hitting for average and power.

Name: Jonah Tong
Report: Tong is a great athlete with a plus fastball-changeup mix. A complicated delivery and iffy breaking ball projection cloud his long-term projection.

Name: Jake Bloss
Report: Bloss has a riding mid-90s fastball and a great pair of breaking balls that he was just starting to harness before he blew out. He had surgery in May of 2025 and should pitch in the second half of 2026.

Name: Tommy Troy
Report: A bounce-back year on both sides of the ball has Troy tracking like a regular at second base with a multi-positional utility fallback if the bat falls short.

Name: Max Clark
Report: Clark is a five-tool talent and is the top center field prospect in baseball.

Name: Bryce Eldridge
Report: Eldridge is an enormous power-hitting first base prospect whose swing is already geared to get to his tremendous raw thunder.

Name: George Lombard Jr.
Report: Lombard is an acrobatic shortstop defender with a chance to hit for power.

Name: George Klassen
Report: Klassen has always had big stuff, and now he's hitting the zone often enough to project him as a good five-and-dive type.

Name: LuJames Groover
Report: Groover is developing into a capable defender at a few infield positions and hits enough to play an integral part-time role.

Name: Kevin McGonigle
Report: McGonigle arguably has the best hit tool in the minor leagues, and he projects to have above-average game power. He's one of the top prospects in baseball, even if he has to slide off shortstop.

Name: Colt Emerson
Report: Emerson has electric hitting hands and should be an everyday infielder. Despite our initial hesitance, his chances of hitting for power and staying at short have improved year over year.

Name: Connelly Early
Report: An elite competitor with a deceptively good fastball, Early is a big league-ready mid-rotation starter.

Name: Nolan McLean
Report: McLean is the best pitching prospect in baseball, and he dominated in his initial big league audition.

Name: Cooper Ingle
Report: Ingle is an athletic catcher with great contact skills, and his exchange on throws is fast enough to make up for a lack of pure arm strength.

Name: Brandon Sproat
Report: Sproat's delivery changed in 2025 and his changeup quality evaporated. If he can get back to the way he looked from 2020-2024, he'll be a big part of the Brewers rotation soon.

Name: Rhett Lowder
Report: Lowder is a fourth starter prospect who attacks east/west with a sinker and slider.

Name: Travis Bazzana
Report: The first overall pick in the 2024 draft, Bazzana is a small-ish second baseman who is a good bet to be an average everyday player, but probably not a star.

Name: JJ Wetherholt
Report: Wetherholt is a bit too bulky and tightly-wound to stick at short, but he has the hit-and-power combination to be a star at the keystone.

Name: Ryan Waldschmidt
Report: Waldschmidt is a well-rounded corner bat with 30-homer upside.

Name: Tommy White
Report: Tommy White's skill set is similar to Maikel Franco's.

Name: Kaelen Culpepper
Report: Culpepper is an acrobatic, if unrefined, defender at short who is already realizing his 20-homer power despite persistent chase issues.

Name: Carson Benge
Report: Benge has one of the sweetest swings in the minors and a shot to be a five-tool player, though he lacks any one elite tool.

Name: Hagen Smith
Report: Smith's compact arm stroke offers one of the best left-handed fastball/slider combos in the minors, but he has only thrown a starter-level of strikes in his draft year at Arkansas.

Name: Konnor Griffin
Report: Griffin is a freaky five-tool superstar with big power and enough contact ability to weaponize it. He's also incredibly fast and has quickly developed into a plus shortstop. He's about to be one of the best young players in the game.

Name: Gage Jump
Report: Jump made strike-throwing improvements and demonstrated 100-inning stamina in 2025, putting him on track to be a fastball-heavy mid-rotation starter.

Name: Braden Montgomery
Report: Montgomery is a yoked switch-hitting outfielder who mashed in college and touts huge bat speed, but he has enough swing-and-miss that there's bust potential.

Name: Trey Yesavage
Report: Yesavage has an elite splitter and carved up some of the best hitters on the planet during an incredible 2025 postseason run.

Name: Payton Tolle
Report: Tolle's a huge, boxy guy with a monster fastball. The development of his secondaries will determine where he best fits in the rotation long-term.

Name: Kade Anderson
Report: Maybe the best pitcher in the 2025 draft, Anderson projects as a quick-moving mid-rotation starter with a great breaking ball.

Name: Jesús Made
Report: Made is a do-it-all, wunderkind infielder with a shot to develop plus contact, power, and defense. He's the odds on favorite to be the sport's top prospect a year from now.

Name: Leo De Vries
Report: De Vries projects to stay at short and could hit 30 homers at maturity. His ceiling is very high.

Name: Franklin Arias
Report: Arias projects as a plus defender at short with a plus hit tool, making him one of the highest-floored prospects in the game.

Name: Eli Willits
Report: Willits was the top pick in the 2025 draft because of his defense, contact feel, and youth. He projects as a good leadoff hitter and plus defender.

Name: Josue De Paula
Report: De Paula has an ideal slugging corner outfield frame paired with a good batting eye, but he has yet to fully actualize his massive power potential.

Name: Alfredo Duno
Report: Duno is a tooled-up catcher with big power and incredible athleticism for a guy his size. He's likely to be a slower developmental burn than other elite prospects, but he has massive long-term ceiling.

Name: Luis Peña
Report: Peña is a twitchy, projectable infielder with a chance for an average bat and plus game power. He probably isn't a shortstop, though.

Name: Rainiel Rodriguez
Report: Built like a short-levered Michelin man, Rodriguez bashed his way into affiliated ball with precocious pull power, and has the tools and smarts to stick behind the plate.

Name: Bryce Rainer
Report: Rainer was a two-way high school player whose stock took off as a shortstop fairly late during the pre-draft process. He was hitting with power in 2025 before he hurt his shoulder and required surgery.

Name: Aidan Miller
Report: Miller is a well-rounded shortstop prospect with uncommon power.

Name: Sebastian Walcott
Report: Walcott looked like he was joining the Tatis Cinematic Universe in 2023 and 2024, but had only a fair 2025 and then got hurt.

Name: Walker Jenkins
Report: Jenkins is an oft-injured outfielder with an excellent approach and contact feel, and he's improved in center field. He doesn't have the power of a superstar player and looks more like if Jesse Winker could play better defense.

Name: Caleb Bonemer
Report: Bonemer is unlikely to stick at short, but the Michigan prep star already looked like a polished all-around bat in his first full season of pro ball.

Name: Ralphy Velazquez
Report: Velazquez broke out in 2025 and now projects as a regular first baseman with 30-homer upside and a good approach.

Name: Eduardo Quintero
Report: Quintero is a fine center field defender with a lovely gap-to-gap approach. If he can start turning on the baseball more frequently, he might end up with enough power to be a 55- or 60-grade prospect a year from now.

Name: Josuar Gonzalez
Report: The top prospect in the DSL last year, Gonzalez projects as an above-average hitter and defender at short.

Name: Ethan Salas
Report: Salas had an early-career breakout, but has either struggled or been injured for the last couple of seasons.

Name: Arjun Nimmala
Report: Nimmala is a physical shortstop with power, but also hit tool risk.

Name: Jonny Farmelo
Report: Farmelo's raw power and speed give him immense potential if he can continue to refine his swing in pro ball. Injuries have limited his ability to get going and threaten his chances to stay in center.

Name: Jefferson Rojas
Report: Rojas is a young middle infield prospect with a great looking swing and increasingly slick shortstop defense.

Name: Emil Morales
Report: Young, twitchy, and explosive, Morales is one of the highest-variance prospects in baseball. You can dream on a 25-homer shortstop.

Name: Charlie Condon
Report: With two hand injuries in the rear-view mirror, it's time for Condon to prove he can tap into the plus-plus power that made him such a coveted amateur prospect.

Name: Zyhir Hope
Report: Hope is a risky corner outfielder with serious hit tool questions, but also 40-homer upside if everything clicks.

Name: Lazaro Montes
Report: Montes has a classic power-hitting profile. He's among the bigger boom-bust types in the sport.

Name: Yolfran Castillo
Report: Castillo is an exciting young hitter with a rare combination of contact ability and physical projection.

Name: Jhonny Level
Report: Level was arguably the best prospect in the ACL last year. He isn't a big guy, but he can hit, has sneaky power, and projects to stay at short.

Name: Michael Arroyo
Report: Arroyo is a short-levered, power-hitting second baseman with a good approach and a shaky glove.

Name: Felnin Celesten
Report: Celesten is a physical, switch-hitting middle infield prospect. Brimming with potential, injuries have limited his chances to develop baseball skills alongside his enviable tools.

Name: Dax Kilby
Report: Kilby's 2025 pro debut reinforced pre-existing confidence that he could hit, and he also looked better playing shortstop than he did in high school. He now looks like a shrewd selection.

Name: Eduardo Tait
Report: Tait is a power-hitting catcher with a laser arm and a concerning lack of plate discipline.

Name: Aiva Arquette
Report: Arquette is an ultra passive hitter with rare size and thump for a shortstop, though he didn't hit for power in his post-draft sample.

Name: Edward Florentino
Report: Florentino is a young power-hitting prospect. Defensively, he's likely to wind up in a corner.

Name: Jett Williams
Report: Williams is a compact little speedster with surprising power for his size. He is still searching the 2B/SS/CF triangle for a comfortable defensive home.

Name: Roldy Brito
Report: A young spark plug with speed and sneaky power, Brito is tooled up and has a chance to be very good at multiple spots around the diamond. To call him a super-utility prospect almost doesn't do him justice.

Name: Jacob Reimer
Report: Reimer is a well-rounded hitter who projects as an everyday third baseman.

Name: Blake Mitchell
Report: Mitchell is an athletic catcher who has grown defensively since draft day. A broken hamate last year has clouded his projection at the plate, where he looks like a power-over-hit player.

Name: Thayron Liranzo
Report: Liranzo has huge power and big questions to answer on both sides of the ball after a rough ride at Double-A in 2025.

Name: Josue Briceño
Report: Briceño is a well-rounded hitter who reached Double-A in 2025. He's still catching some, but he's probably going to be a first baseman or DH.

Name: Ethan Holliday
Report: Holliday has absurd raw power and a long swing that has limited his ability to make consistent contact. He might need an adjustment to break out, and he has 40-homer ceiling if he does.

Name: Jansel Luis
Report: Luis is a projectable switch-hitting shortstop with big bat speed. His tendency to chase makes him a volatile prospect.

Name: JD Dix
Report: Dix is a power-hitting lefty infield prospect who may not have the arm to stay at shortstop.

Name: Demetrio Crisantes
Report: Crisantes is a relatively undersized 2B/1B prospect who had a sizzling 2024 on the Complex and in the Cal League. His statistics -- both his surface level performance and his underlying contact and power data -- are robust, the sort one might associate with a potential everydya player. But Crisantes isn't an especially projectable athlete and aspects of his swing indicate he might struggle with better fastballs as he climbs, and so here he's forecast as a second-division type in the Tadahito Iguchi mold.

Name: Mike Sirota
Report: Speedy, power-over-hit center field prospect with plus plate discipline. Tightly wound athlete with narrow build, wiry and strong. Hands are especially lively with low-ball power. Likely going to swing underneath a ton of in-zone fastballs and be a below-average contact hitter. Speed fits in center; reads and routes need polish but the footspeed is there. Projected issues with the hit tool and Sirota's flavor of build/athleticism look more like a part-timer. His on-base ability buoys his profile and gives Sirota a shot to be a Tyrone Taylor type of complimentary outfielder.

Name: Kayson Cunningham
Report: Cunningham had arugably the bets pure hit tool in the 2025 draft. He's a smaller player whose future will be influenced by how strong he can become.

Name: Cam Collier
Report: Collier walked a unique amateur path en route to a signing bonus as large and impressive as his power and arm strength.

Name: James Tibbs III
Report: Tibbs currently has the look of a good platoon outfielder. His projection could shift into more of an everyday role if his defense improves and/or he shows he can hit upper-level lefties.

Name: Roc Riggio
Report: The Yankees made changes to Riggio's swing in 2025 (bigger leg kick) that made his entire operation more athletic and improved his plate coverage. His high end outcome is a Rougie Odor sequel.

Name: Joendry Vargas
Report: I hope that you're the one. If not, you are the prototype.

Name: Adriel Radney
Report: Radney dealt with back issues during his first pro season and will likely repeat the DSL in 2025. He has the tools and projection of a first round high school prospect.

Name: Jeral Perez
Report: Perez is a stocky 2B/3B prospect without a ton of physical projection. Some aspects of his hit tool are good (he's short to the ball, contact is top-hand driven), while others are bad (he lacks great barrel control), and his defense is also a mixed bag. He has a puncher's chance to be a regular at second base and produce akin to the way Brendan Rodgers has so far.

Name: Slade Caldwell
Report: Caldwell is a short (but not small) outfield prospect with blazing speed and a swing geared for airborne contact. How he develops physically (he's already so muscular that his frame is maxed out) and he way it will impact his skillset is hard to predict.

Name: Yassel Soler
Report: Soler has a skillset similar to Ty France. He's a chase prone corner infielder with plus bat speed and a swing that's not yet actualized for lift and power.

Name: Samuel Zavala
Report: Of the teenage hitters on the list, Zavala's feel to hit is probably the most polished.

Name: Cristofer Torin
Report: Torin's contact data has been pretty nutty since he entered pro ball but his complete lack of power caps his ceiling, and inconsisent defense clouds his would-be part time role.

Name: Druw Jones
Report: Jones is a potential Michael A. Taylor type of outfielder, with great defense, power projection, and likely too many strikeouts to play every day.

Name: Gavin Conticello
Report: Conticello projects as a corner platoon bat with power but shaky plate coverage. He has a classic low-ball lefty swing and he'll need to do a lot of damage on pitches in that region to profile.

Name: Nick Mitchell
Report: Mitchell is an undersized corner outfielder who posted premium contact rates in college and during a brief post-draft run with Dunedin. He lacks prototypical corner outfield power, but it's possible his 2024 output was muted by a preseason hand injury.

Name: Alberto Barriga
Report: Barriga is a very fun little catcher with rare speed and contact ability. Basically no everyday catchers are this small, and so he projects as a backup.

Name: Christian Cerda
Report: Cerda is a backup catching prospect who should grow into above-average power as his frame matures into his mid-20s.

Name: Thomas White
Report: White is one of a few minor league pitchers whose pitches played like plus or better offerings across the board in 2025. He lacks precise feel for command, but might be too overwhelming for that to matter very much. He has no. 2 starter upside.

Name: Seth Hernandez
Report: Hernandez is one of the better high school pitchers of the last decade, a freak athlete who'll touch 100 with ease before finishing hitters with a great changeup. His breaking ball and control need polish.

Name: Ryan Sloan
Report: Sloan was one of the top arms in the low minors last year. He could have three plus pitches at maturity.

Name: Liam Doyle
Report: Doyle is a superb athlete who broke out in his draft year at Tennessee thanks to a 70-grade fastball, with enough fledgling feel for his secondaries to stick as a starter.

Name: Jarlin Susana
Report: Susana has one of the planet's nastiest sliders and touches 103. He'll miss the first half of 2026 recovering from lat surgery.

Name: Tyler Bremner
Report: A 70 changeup highlights a relatively safe, no. 3 projection for Bremner. Blink and he'll be in the Angels rotation.

Name: Carlos Lagrange
Report: Lagrange has a big arm and could have two plus-plus pitches in relief. We're projecting him as a closer.

Name: Luis De León
Report: De León has easy mid-90s lefty velo and a suite of plus secondaries, but he's good for one stretch of losing the strike zone per season.

Name: Caden Scarborough
Report: Scarborough is a lanky, projectable righty with a plus fastball/sweeper combo. He took a leap as a strike-thrower in 2025.

Name: Brody Hopkins
Report: Hopkins only began pitching in a serious way during his draft spring. The Mariners traded him for Randy Arozarena, and Hopkins has become a hard-throwing power pitcher with a nasty cutter under the Rays' tutelage.

Name: Michael Forret
Report: Forret is a command-oriented starter whose pitch execution allows his modest stuff to play up. He's a pitchability no. 4 starter prospect.

Name: Jack Wenninger
Report: Wenninger found more velocity last year; he now projects as a no. 4 starter.

Name: David Davalillo
Report: Davalillo is a crafty starter prospect with great secondary stuff, led by his plus-plus splitter.

Name: Khal Stephen
Report: Stephen throws a ton of strikes and has plus command of mostly average stuff.

Name: Jurrangelo Cijntje
Report: Cijntje has a shot to be a switch-pitcher, but his righty stuff might be good enough on its own to make him a mid-rotation starter.

Name: Jaxon Wiggins
Report: Wiggins has one of the more dominant fastballs in the minors, and his changeup has improved in pro ball. Can he stay healthy and throw enough strikes to start?

Name: Christian Oppor
Report: Oppor is an athletic JUCO lefty who has two bat-missing secondaries and has touched 100 mph, but he has a limited track record of strikes and performance.

Name: Travis Sykora
Report: Sykora is an enormous, hard-throwing righty with an excellent splitter who is currently on the shelf with injury. He looked like a potential no. 2/3 starter when healthy.

Name: Moisés Chace
Report: Chace has a monster uphill fastball that should enable him to play a prominent role, even if his command doesn't develop enough for him to start.

Name: Kyson Witherspoon
Report: Kyson's command (especially of his fastball) backed up in his first pro season, creating even more relief risk than he had at Oklahoma.

Name: Garrett Hawkins
Report: Hawkins returned from TJ in 2025 and had added velocity to his already trait-friendly fastball. He had a season that put him in line for a Padres roster spot as a middle reliever.

Name: Griffin Herring
Report: The Yankees made several changes to Herrin after drafting him (more sliders, better extension, higher arm slot) and the result looks like a stable backend starter despite 30-grade fastball velocity.

Name: Yordin Chalas
Report: Chalas is a super athletic young relief prospect who has a chance to pitch in the back of a bullpen one day.

Name: Yu-Min Lin
Report: Lin has great arm speed but his command is not as sharp as one would hope for a guy who sits 91. He looks like a 5th starter.

Name: Caden Grice
Report: Grice was a college two-way player who shifted o pitching full time in 2024. He blew out and needed TJ. He has the build and stuff of a solid backend starter.

Name: Yujanyer Herrera
Report: Herrera is a crafty young righty with a plus slider and command projection. He's closer to 240 pounds or than his listed weight of 175.

Name: Josh Grosz
Report: Swingman/fifth starter prospect with a tough-to-time delivery and an improving changeup.

Name: Jacob Steinmetz
Report: Steinmetz's strike-throwing took a step forward in 2024 and he's tracking like a fifth starter.

Name: Griff McGarry
Report: McGarry has three plus pitches but also the worst control on the Top 100.

Name: Spencer Giesting
Report: Giesting is a deceptive lefty with a delivery atypical of a starter. Here he's projected o be a solid long reliever.

Name: Yoniel Curet
Report: Curet was the minor league strikeout leader over the last couple of years and has held upper-90s velo for 120 innings. His changeup appeared to be taking off late in 2024.

Name: Dylan Ray
Report: Ray is a below-average athlete with below-average command bu he has the stuff to pitch in a roation if he can polish that up.

Name: Joe Elbis
Report: Elbis is a skinny backend starter prospect with a good slider.
